keyAndScale.modalCharacter: G Major with Parallel Minor Borrowed iv Chord (G Minor / Modal Mixture)

scalesUsed.name: G Major Scale (Ionian)
scalesUsed.notes: G - A - B - C - D - E - F#
scalesUsed.application: The bright diatonic framework for the G and C major chords in the verse

scalesUsed.name: G Natural Minor (Aeolian)
scalesUsed.notes: G - A - Bb - C - D - Eb - F
scalesUsed.application: The source of the heart-wrenching borrowed C minor (iv) chord

scalesUsed.name: B Harmonic Minor
scalesUsed.notes: B - C# - D - D# - E - F# - G
scalesUsed.application: Provides the D# leading tone that turns the diatonic Bm into a dramatic B major chord

mainProgression.description: The ultimate 4-chord demonstration of modal interchange: moving from the triumphant C major (IV) to the devastating, borrowed C minor (iv)

sectionProgressions.description: Two bars each of G, B, C, and Cm repeating throughout the entire song with dynamic evolution from clean arpeggios to roaring fuzz
Johnny Greenwood's famous pre-chorus assault: three violent muted pick-hand rakes into the fretboard that launch the chorus

harmonicFunction: G (I) - The warm, gentle home tonic chord played with clean arpeggiated fingerpicking
B (III) - Major III chord (secondary dominant V of vi) creating unexpected upward tension with the sharp D# note
C (IV) - The subdominant lift that provides a fleeting sense of hopeful brightness
Cm (iv) - The emotional gut-punch: borrowed from G minor, the Eb note creates profound longing and sorrow before resolving to G

techniques.name: Modal Interchange Voice Leading (IV to iv)
techniques.description: Understanding and executing the single-note chromatic descent from E (in C major) to Eb (in C minor) to D (in G major)

notes: Only one note changes between C and Cm: the 3rd drops from E to Eb
That single half-step descent carries 90% of the song's emotional weight
Emphasize the G string fret 5 (E) moving to fret 4 (Eb) when playing barre chords
sequence: Fret full C major barre chord on fret 3 or fret 8
Lift middle finger to flatten the 3rd to Eb for Cm
Let the Eb ring out before resolving to D on the G chord
tips: Listen intently to the chromatic descent: E -> Eb -> D
Play Cm with delicate restraint in the verse to maximize its emotional impact

techniques.name: Dead-String Crunch Rakes
techniques.description: Johnny Greenwood's iconic aggressive pre-chorus dead-note strums created by muting strings with the fretting hand while digging in with heavy distortion

notes: Greenwood originally played these rakes in frustration because he hated how quiet the song was
Turn on high-gain Marshall ShredMaster distortion pedal
Rest all 4 fretting fingers across the strings without pressing to fretboard
Deliver three violent down-up-down power strums
sequence: Clean verse arpeggio finishes on Cm
Strike three explosive percussive rakes: CHUG-CHUG-CHUG
Slam into full G major chorus
tips: Attack the strings with authority right above the bridge pickup
Ensure zero open strings ring out accidentally

techniques.name: Clean Steady Arpeggio Picking
techniques.description: Ed O'Brien's continuous clean 8th-note arpeggiated picking pattern outlining the barre chords throughout the verses

notes: Held using full 6th-string and 5th-string barre chord grips
Ascending and descending picking pattern across the middle strings
Keeps the rhythm floating steadily at 92 BPM
sequence: Pick low E, then D, G, B strings in steady rhythm
Shift cleanly to B major barre chord (fret 7)
tips: Keep the pick close to the strings to minimize wasted motion
Maintain consistent volume on every picked note

sections.name: Clean Intro & Verse 1 Arpeggios
sections.description: The serene clean guitar arpeggio pattern introducing the G - B - C - Cm progression with gentle compression and subtle room reverb.
notes: Use clean barre chord grips at fret 3 (G), fret 7 (B), fret 8 (C), and fret 8 (Cm)
Pick in steady eighth notes across strings 6, 4, 3, and 2
Listen for the poignant drop from C major to C minor

sections.name: Pre-Chorus Dead-Note Crunch Rakes
sections.description: Johnny Greenwood's legendary three muted string stabs with roaring distortion that shatter the calm and launch the chorus.
notes: Deaden all strings with the fretting hand
Engage high-gain Marshall ShredMaster distortion
Strike three aggressive, percussive downstrokes right on the beat

sections.name: Chorus 1 Fuzz Wall of Sound ('I'm a creep')
sections.technique: Modal Interchange Voice Leading (IV to iv)
sections.description: A monumental wall of distorted guitars playing full, ringing open and barre chords through the G - B - C - Cm progression.
notes: Heavy full-strum downstrokes with maximum distortion sustain
The transition from C to Cm sounds colossal under high gain
Let the low root notes ring out thunderously

sections.name: Verse 2 Delicate Clean Arpeggiation
sections.description: The song drops back to near-silence for the second verse as Thom Yorke sings 'She's running out the door'.
notes: Soft picking dynamics creating extreme contrast with the chorus
Emphasize the flat 3rd (Eb) in the Cm chord
Maintain relaxed 92 BPM pulse

sections.name: Bridge Vocal Climax & High Arpeggio Ascents
sections.description: Thom Yorke's soaring vocal peak ('She runs, runs, runs...') backed by swelling tremolo-picked electric chords.
notes: Swell chords with pick strokes building in velocity
Let the emotional shift between C and Cm ring with sustain
Brace for Johnny Greenwood's final explosive guitar entry

sections.name: Chorus 2 & Outro Decaying Clean Cadence
sections.description: The explosive final chorus dissolves into the gentle, mournful piano and clean arpeggios of the outro.
notes: Gradually fade right-hand strumming intensity
Allow the final borrowed C minor chord to linger
Resolve cleanly onto the home G major chord to end

guitar.recommended: Fender Telecaster Plus (with Lace Sensor pickups) or standard Telecaster / Stratocaster
alternatives: Any humbucker or P90 electric guitar
guitar.pickup: Bridge Lace Sensor Dually humbucker for the explosive crunch

amp.recommended: Fender Twin Reverb (Clean) paired with a Marshall 8080 Valvestate (Distortion)

effects.distortion: Marshall ShredMaster or ProCo Rat distortion pedal set to maximum saturation
effects.reverb: Fender spring reverb on the clean channel (setting 4)
effects.other: Boss Tremolo and Roland Space Echo for ambient textures

beginner.title: The 4-Chord Progression
steps: Learn the 4 core chords: G, B, C, and Cm using barre chord shapes
Practice transitioning smoothly from C to Cm at 60 BPM
Listen to and feel the emotional power of the modal mixture

intermediate.title: Clean Arpeggio Picking & Dead-Note Crunch
steps: Master the clean 8th-note arpeggiated picking pattern at 92 BPM
Nail the timing and explosive attack of the 3 pre-chorus dead-note rakes
Transition seamlessly between clean arpeggios and roaring chorus fuzz

advanced.title: Dynamic Mastery & Studio Nuance
steps: Recreate Johnny Greenwood's dual-amp clean/dirty rig setup
Master the extreme quiet-to-loud dynamics that define 90s alternative rock
Perform the song with authentic vocal emotion and guitar intensity

commonMistakes: Missing the C to Cm chord change and staying on C major
Playing open chord voicings instead of barre chords, losing the smooth voice leading
Rushing the tempo during the quiet verses
practiceRoutine: 5 min: C to Cm barre chord transition drill focusing on the flat-3rd drop
10 min: Clean arpeggio picking pattern with metronome at 92 BPM
15 min: Pre-chorus dead-note rake and chorus explosion transition practice
10 min: Full song playthrough focusing on extreme dynamic contrast
focusAreas: Modal interchange voice leading (E -> Eb -> D)
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 92 BPM with a steady 4/4 click
Practice the verse arpeggio pattern until every eighth note lands exactly on the grid
Practice the 3 pre-chorus dead-note rakes so they land squarely on beats 3, 3&, and 4
